key_insight: SigmaMedStat improves ICU false-alarm triage by modeling physiological signals over time, with a chunked CWT + EfficientNet + LSTM approach outperforming a static baseline.
clinical_relevance: Better alarm filtering could reduce alarm fatigue in ICUs and help staff focus faster on truly urgent events.
method: Split each 60-second ICU recording into six 10-second chunks
Convert each chunk into Continuous Wavelet Transform scalograms and encode them with a shared EfficientNet-B0
Feed the chunk features into a two-layer LSTM for final alarm classification
evidence_signal: On 498 four-channel ICU alarm recordings from PhysioNet/Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2015, five-fold stratified cross-validation produced mean AUC 0.822 ± 0.016 versus 0.641 for a static EfficientNet baseline.
watch_item: Performance varied by alarm type and the model still produced false negatives, so real-world deployment would need careful validation and safety review.
paper_title: SigmaMedStat: Temporal Signal Modeling for ICU False Alarm Reduction
